Resolve two quotient bits per combinational divider stage
motivation:
The baseline runs at a median 5.442 MHz. Its reported 199.837 ns path traverses
operand forwarding and the EX ALU. The signed and unsigned division and remainder
operators in alu.sv are the strongest candidates for that depth. A shorter
combinational divider could raise Fmax even on cycles executing an ordinary ADD.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU with one unrolled radix-4 magnitude divider
in the existing EX cycle. Each of 16 stages consumes the next two dividend bits
and produces two quotient bits. For trial remainder T = 4*R + next_pair,
form T-D, T-2D and T-3D in parallel. Use their borrow bits to select the
largest fitting multiple and its already-computed difference, passing T through
for digit zero. This halves the number of dependent digit decisions relative
to a binary restoring divider. The tradeoff is routing three candidates into
each remainder mux. With the same instruction latencies and stall sequence,
the bracketed cycle count should stay at 4,491,485. A median above 5.70 MHz
at that count would clear the tournament threshold.

changes.description:
In the real-arithmetic branch, convert signed operands to unsigned magnitudes
and precompute D, 2D and 3D once with 34-bit precision. Stage i (1 through 16)
needs only 2*i trial bits because it has consumed that many dividend bits.
Flag any multiple with bits above that width as too large, then use a
zero-extended subtraction for each low-width difference and borrow. Assemble
the quotient from the selected digits and use the final remainder directly.
For signed operations, negate the quotient when operand signs differ and
give the remainder the dividend's sign. Handle zero divisor before output
sign correction (all-ones quotient, original dividend as remainder) and
preserve INT_MIN/-1 results (INT_MIN, zero). Retain the existing ALTOPS
expressions and combinational ALU interface.

title: Move DIV and REM to a shared four-pass divider
motivation:
The 5.442 MHz baseline takes 4,491,485 cycles for ten CoreMark iterations.
Gowin reports a 199.837 ns, 156-cell path through forwarding and the EX ALU.
The ALU evaluates full-width signed and unsigned division and remainder
combinationally. Their serial quotient decisions are the likeliest source
of this depth. Disassembly of the canonical RV32IM -O3 ELF shows five
DIVU instructions, all in main. The measured start_time/iterate/stop_time
sequence executes none of them, and the ELF contains no DIV, REM or REMU.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Give EX one blocking divider for DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU. Latch forwarded
operands on issue, divide their unsigned magnitudes with eight restoring
quotient-bit steps per clock for four clocks, then select and sign-correct
the quotient or remainder. Use the subtraction borrow to select the next
remainder at each step. The register between passes cuts the full-width
recurrence out of the one-cycle ALU path. Only division and remainder add
issue stalls, so matrix multiplies and ordinary integer dependencies can
sustain their current issue rate.

Expect nearly the same marker-bracketed cycle count. Extra divide cycles
during setup can shift the phase of the pseudo-random bus stalls. At the
baseline cycle count, 8.163 MHz would yield a 50% fitness gain. Even with
2% more cycles, 5.81 MHz would clear the 4.6% acceptance margin. Compare
median Gowin Fmax and bracketed cycles separately to test this prediction.

title: Predict direct branches with a 64-entry agree predictor at fetch
motivation:
The baseline fetches PC+4 until EX resolves a transfer. Since IF feeds ID
combinationally, a taken branch or jump discards one younger fetch slot.
A reference trace between the CoreMark markers contains 529,588 conditional
branches, of which 294,425 change the successor, plus 49,367 direct jumps.
The baseline's 199.837 ns worst path crosses forwarding and the EX ALU.
Predicting these direct transfers in IF can save cycles with a small table.

hypothesis.motivation:
The baseline fetches PC+4 until EX resolves a transfer. Since IF feeds ID

A reference trace between the CoreMark markers contains 529,588 conditional

The baseline's 199.837 ns worst path crosses forwarding and the EX ALU.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Index 64 two-bit saturating counters with fetch PC[7:2]. Use the offset
sign as the default direction for a legal conditional branch (backward
taken, forward fall-through). Predict taken = offset_sign XOR counter[1].
The counter learns whether to invert the default, so a hot backedge and
a usually untaken forward guard can share an entry constructively. Predict
direct JAL taken. Compute the signed B/J target in parallel with the table
lookup and select it only for a word-aligned address in instruction RAM.
Use PC+4 for every other fetch, including JALR. Carry the selected direction
bit with the accepted instruction. Direct targets are exact by construction,
so EX can detect a miss by comparing this bit with the resolved direction.
A miss redirects to the resolved next PC and kills the younger instruction.
Correct predictions let the successor enter ID/EX immediately. An isolated
RTL prototype completed ten 2K CoreMark iterations in 4,194,484 bracketed
cycles with both bus stalls enabled, versus 4,491,485 on the baseline.
All five CRCs matched. Gowin reported 5.214, 5.486 and 5.486 MHz across
the three placement options. The median gives 13.08 iter/s, a 7.9% gain
over 12.12. The prototype used 12 LUT-RAM primitives versus 8 at baseline.

title: Shorten the divider feedback path to five quotient bits per clock
motivation:
The 31.773 MHz champion's reported 36.737 ns worst path runs from quotient_q[31]
to remainder_q[11] through eight dependent subtract-and-select steps. The timed
CoreMark loop executes no DIV or REM, so spending three more clocks on those
instructions can buy clock frequency for every instruction in the loop.

hypothesis.motivation:

to remainder_q[11] through eight dependent subtract-and-select steps. The timed
CoreMark loop executes no DIV or REM, so spending three more clocks on those
instructions can buy clock frequency for every instruction in the loop.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retune the existing blocking divider to compute five binary quotient bits per
clock over seven passes. Feed it three leading zero dividend bits so every pass
uses the same five-step datapath. This removes three serial carry chains and
their remainder muxes from the feedback path. Seven compute clocks also leave
room for issue, transfer and a redirect or load-use bubble within the formal
wrapper's ten-cycle forward-progress window.

Expect close to the champion's 4,491,485 bracketed cycles for ten iterations.
Setup divides can shift the stall generator's phase. At that cycle count a
median Fmax above 33.24 MHz clears the acceptance margin. A 25% gain would
require about 39.72 MHz. The single-cycle multiply path may cap the gain.

title: Predict the next fetch from a 128-entry branch target buffer
motivation:
The champion takes 4,491,485 cycles for ten CoreMark iterations at
31.773 MHz. Every taken transfer discards one younger fetch slot. On the
earlier core, predicting conditional branches and JAL saved 297,001
cycles. Its 5.648 MHz result came from the older combinational-divider
design. The champion's worst path lies inside the four-pass divider.
A PC-indexed branch target buffer (BTB) can supply learned targets in
parallel with instruction fetch and can also cover recurring JALR targets.

hypothesis.motivation:

design. The champion's worst path lies inside the four-pass divider.

parallel with instruction fetch and can also cover recurring JALR targets.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 128-entry direct-mapped BTB for conditional branches, JAL and
JALR. Index it by fetch PC[8:2]. Each entry holds a source tag, an aligned
target word address and a two-bit taken counter. Only allocate aligned
source and target addresses in the 1 MiB instruction RAM, so an 11-bit
tag and 18-bit target suffice. Select the target on a valid tag hit with
the counter MSB set. Otherwise fetch PC+4. Reading a learned target
removes the instruction-to-target addition from the fetch prediction path.

Carry the actual fetch decision into EX. On every valid instruction that
advances, compare its predicted successor with the architectural successor.
This covers loop exits, changing indirect targets and stale entries for
code that has changed. Recover on a mismatch even if imemReady is low.
Correct predictions admit the successor into ID/EX on the next ready slot.

An isolated prototype on the champion completed ten iterations in
4,180,499 bracketed cycles with both bus stalls enabled and all five
CRCs validated. This saves 310,986 cycles. Counting accepted EX
transfers between the markers, the BTB reduced conditional-branch
corrections from 294,425 to 42,359, JAL corrections from 49,367 to
1,849, and JALR corrections from 13,735 to 1,647, relative to
sequential fetch. Gowin reported 30.613, 31.656 and 31.656 MHz
across the three placement options. The median gives 75.72 iterations/s,
7.04% above 70.74. At this cycle count, 30.94 MHz clears the 4.6%
acceptance threshold. The worst path
in placement option zero still ran between divider registers. That
placement used 3,251 logic cells and seven BSRAMs versus 2,844 and six

fast formal checks. Selftest and all three random programs matched

title: Remove EX redirect from register reads and load-use comparison
motivation:
The 46.846 MHz champion reports a 26.981 ns path from EX/MEM.rd through
forwarding, branch resolution, IF and hazard logic to ID/EX.rs1_val.
IF substitutes a NOP on redirect, so the branch decision can change both
register read addresses and the load-use comparison late in the clock.
The redirect also clears the wide ID/EX payload for an instruction that will
never retire.

title: Predict a load's word index from the instruction producing its base
motivation:
The champion supplies 604,950 instructions during fetch waits, yet ten
CoreMark iterations still take 3,408,562 cycles. A load followed by a
consumer incurs an interlock, and a data-bus wait holds both instructions.
A tagged word buffer could deliver the load at the EX/MEM edge if ID
can predict its read index one cycle earlier. In a pointer chase the
preceding load can supply the next base before it reaches the register
file.

title: Predict load-use latency and forward the last formatted result
motivation:
The champion interlocks every consumer directly behind a load. A PC-stride
trial missed 85,446 dependent accesses at just four pointer-chasing load
sites. The actual load address is available in EX, one clock before the
consumer needs the value. Predicting result availability lets that clock
serve as the read latency of a synchronous RAM.

trial missed 85,446 dependent accesses at just four pointer-chasing load
sites. The actual load address is available in EX, one clock before the

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Let each static load predict whether its dependent consumer can issue
immediately. Use 64 one-bit entries indexed by load PC[7:2], initialized
to fast and trained on the last completed load's forwarding hit. A slow
prediction takes the existing load-use bubble. On a fast prediction admit
the consumer, even though the result lookup and its tag check are pending.

Index a 1024-row result buffer in EX using the actual forwarded effective
address. Store the full raw word, the last extracted 32-bit result, its byte
offset, width and signedness, a RAM address tag and validity. The candidate
result reaches the consumer's EX forwarding mux directly from the RAM
output. In parallel, MEM checks the tag, access format, alignment and valid
bit. On a match, the consumer advances and the load completes internally.
On a miss, complete the ordinary demand load. If the admitted consumer
depends on it, hold that consumer through bus waits and then for the edge
that deposits the load in WB. Retry it with WB forwarding. An independent
follower can advance on the demand response edge.

motivation:
Gowin traced the champion's 19.855 ns worst path from the reciprocal
seed ROM to the quotient register. The other round-six operand design
had the same endpoints. Four kinds of divider product and ordinary MUL
all use one 36x36 multiplier, with input steering and a variable shift
on the quotient output. This limits the 71.092 MHz clock even though

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Dedicate one registered-input multiplier to ordinary MUL and give the
blocking divider four separately inferred products with fixed operand
sources. Two products implement the two Newton refinements, one estimates
the quotient, and one computes Q*B for exact correction. While the
reciprocal refines, pre-shift dividend magnitude A by the divisor
exponent k and precompute A-B. The quotient product then feeds a fixed
bit slice. The residual product feeds two parallel subtractors whose
registered outputs supply both possible remainders and the correction
bit. This keeps the seven divide clocks and one multiply issue per clock.

S = 2^34 and r = R/S after refinement. The existing 512-bin seed has
relative error below 1/512 + 2/4096. Each rounded Newton step keeps a
lower bound and maps relative error e to at most e^2 + 3/S. After two
steps, 0 <= 1/D - r < 2^-32. Discarding the low k bits of A costs at
most 1 - 2^-k quotient units, and the reciprocal error on A >> k costs
less than 2^-k. The trial Q is exact or one low. The sign of (A-B)-Q*B
therefore selects the exact quotient and remainder using one correction.

the largest absolute reciprocal error was below 0.589 times 2^-32.

motivation:
The champion takes 3,097,817 cycles for ten CoreMark iterations. Its
reported 19.674 ns worst path runs from the Newton seed ROM to the quotient

the clock for unrelated instructions. The score needs a median above

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the two Newton refinements with one piecewise-linear reciprocal

left endpoint L = (1024+i)/1024. A tangent at L underestimates 1/D.

every unsigned magnitude, including exact multiples.

The split-target experiment reached 80.074 MHz and put EX forwarding and address generation on the path to the RAM write enable. A scratch implementation that queued the writes and stored an absolute direct target preserved all five CRCs and 3,062,533 bracketed cycles, but reached only 76.294 MHz on placement 1. A register between the RAM output and fetch steering could shorten the read path while keeping training writes off the admission path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Look up the existing 512-row successor table one fetch earlier. While fetching A and predicting B, send B's nine index bits to the synchronous read port. During B the RAM presents the row for B, which contains its previously observed successor C and C's instruction. At the edge admitting B, capture this row in fabric flip-flops. During C, the saved instruction, its address and its direct-target metadata are available from those flip-flops. A warm stream still admits one instruction per clock.

The lookup is speculative and internal. Use the low bits of the sequential or predicted direct address without waiting for full target-range validation, EX redirect or the load-use interlock. Check the registered probe index against the actual B index before promoting its response. Keep the full word-address check before issuing C from that response. A bad probe costs a cache opportunity. A ready bus can still supply the instruction immediately. Stage accepted training pairs for one clock so the physical write port takes registered inputs.

The first lookahead prototype completed ten iterations in 3,107,313 bracketed cycles with all five CRCs. At that count the median must exceed 84.162 MHz for promotion. A saved instruction initially timed out across load-use and divide holds. Adding a demand re-read of the last admitted predecessor fixed that case and passed all 38 pipeline tests. The revised design still needs a bracketed CoreMark run and median timing. The main risks are missed probes after redirects and a new timing path into the nine-bit RAM address.

changes.description: Retain the successor-table indexing and agree counters. Give the read port a free-running lookahead index. Carry the sampled index and collision validity with its output. Promote a matching row only for an admitted RAM PC. Preserve a usable response across holds, and if a missing saved word blocks fetch, re-read the last admitted predecessor index, even while admission is stalled. Install its response independently of admission only on a full match to the waiting PC. Cancel that demand response on redirect, invalidation or collision. The last admitted predecessor must survive a redirect so the resolved entry can be trained. Keep the admitted successor word stable across repeated waits. A ready bus word overrides cached data and drives its own B/J prediction. Train from a registered predecessor index, successor PC, bus word and enable. Use the write stage to pack the successor instruction's aligned in-RAM B/J target and eligibility bits. Verify legal JALR steering in EX. Invalidate or forward reads that conflict with a pending or intervening write, including a held probe. Preserve the existing logical same-row collision veto. On reset or an admitted FENCE.I discard pending fills, probes and held responses and let the sweep take priority.

On a direct direction miss, form the recovery PC from the issuing instruction's registered PC and immediate. Choose PC+4 for a predicted-taken miss and the full target for a predicted-fallthrough miss. This lets IF store only the aligned RAM target in a row. title: Steer fetch from the successor RAM and train it from ordered MEM transfers
motivation:
The champion takes 3,062,533 cycles for ten iterations at 79.301 MHz.
On its median placement the saved instruction passes through displacement
decoding, a target adder and a range check on a 17.904 ns path back to
the PC. The path from EX forwarding to the successor RAM is 17.807 ns.
The four-word fetch prototype added 44,559 cycles. The existing one-word
RAM already delivers an aligned successor address in time to steer JALR.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move direct-control steering across the synchronous successor lookup.
When fetch admits P, read the existing 512-entry table at P[10:2],
register P+4 and register a one-bit request to use the returned address.
Request it for a legal JAL or JALR and for a legal branch whose agree
counter predicts taken. On the following cycle select the registered
row's successor PC on a qualified response, or P+4 on a miss. The
fetched instruction no longer drives an offset adder on the next-PC
path. The row continues to supply its word during instruction-bus waits.
A ready bus word takes priority. A held fetch retains both its PC and
its row until the consumer advances.

Train the same row format from consecutive advancing EX/MEM entries.
Remember the older instruction's PC index across bubbles. When the
next valid instruction leaves MEM, its PC and word form the payload
for that index. This records the actual edge through branches and
indirect jumps and takes the current EX redirect and load-use
interlock off the RAM write port. Only aligned RAM PCs participate.
Suppress colliding reads and clear the pending predecessor on reset
and FENCE.I so a delayed pair cannot restore an invalidated word.

EX verifies the PC actually selected for a taken transfer against its
full RV32IM target. A forecast on a non-taken or faulting branch can
recover to P+4. Preserve JALR bit-zero clearing, link suppression on
faults and redirect priority over an instruction wait. Aliasing may
steer a fetch but a saved instruction requires its full PC to match
the selected fetch address. Only the resolved path can retire or
issue a store.

A scratch implementation with MEM-pair training completed all ten
iterations with both buses stalling, all five canonical CRCs and
3,083,798 bracketed cycles, a 0.69% cycle cost.
At that count the promotion threshold is 83.53 MHz. An 85 MHz median
would give 275.6 iterations/s. EX target verification and the
successor read enable are the remaining timing risks.

title: Probe both carry outcomes of a predicted load address
motivation:
The early load predictor uses XOR for the word index. A base of 68 and
displacement of 4 therefore probe the resident word at 64 even though
the consumer needs 72. EX then puts forwarded rs1, a full-width address
addition and a hit check on the path to fetch admission. A scratch
predictor with a full-width base hint and one address adder saved
4,954 cycles, but Gowin placement 1 reached only 77.574 MHz. Its
longest path ran from the saved fetch word to the predictor's
address-eligibility register. The cycle gain alone is 0.16%.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the existing 1,024-word load buffer into two 512-word banks selected
by byte-address bit 6. Probe both possible outcomes of the carry out of
bit 5. Both reads use the existing pointer hint, including the unchecked
word from an immediately preceding load. Retain just the hint's low 12
bits. The carry selects a registered RAM response and need not propagate
through the upper index adder before either read can start. A fill or
store occupies only its addressed bank, so the other candidate can still
be available on that cycle.

In ID let b be the 12-bit base hint, d the I-immediate bits, and L the
seven-bit unsigned sum of b[5:0] and d[5:0]. The bank that supplies the
candidate is b[6] XOR d[6] XOR L[6]. Both row indices end in L[5:2].
Compute their upper five bits in parallel by adding b[11:7] and d[11:7].
The even bank adds (b[6] OR d[6]) to that sum, and the odd bank adds
(b[6] AND d[6]). Keep the sixth sum bit for each bank. The selected
sixth bit must equal d[11] for the signed addition to stay in the
base's 4 KiB page. Register these flags and the bank choice alongside
the low base hint and alignment information.

For a same-page prediction the returned RAM tag identifies the required
base page. Verify the actual rs1 against {12'b0, selected_tag, saved_b}
in EX. Compare the physical operand sources in parallel and qualify the
results with the existing forwarding selects. This checks all 32 bits
and removes the resolved address adder from the early-hit decision.
A cross-page displacement, wrong base, unavailable bank or collision
uses the existing interlock and the independent resolved-address probe
in MEM. A scratch two-bank implementation completed ten CoreMark
iterations in 3,057,579 bracketed cycles with both buses stalling.
All five CRCs matched. An exhaustive check of all 16,777,216 base-low
and displacement pairs reproduced the word index and page-crossing
decision. At that cycle count promotion requires more than 82.815 MHz.
The two-bank median Fmax is unmeasured. The main timing risks are routing
the two RAM responses and the independent fetch-PC path.

title: Register the divider product before residual correction
motivation:
On the champion's 83.645 MHz median placement, Gowin reports 17.250 ns
from the reciprocal ROM through the shared DSP to residual_q and 17.244 ns
from residual_q into the signed divide result register. Pass 6 puts a
32-bit subtractor after the DSP. The following cycle can compare, subtract
and negate in series. CoreMark executes no divides in its timed loop,
but both paths constrain the clock on every instruction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the seven-pass Newton schedule and retime its final correction. Let
A and B be the dividend and divisor magnitudes, Q the existing quotient
estimate and P = Q*B. For B > 0 the estimate is exact or one low, so
P fits in 32 bits. The correction test A-P >= B is equivalent to
A >= B and P <= A-B. Precompute A-B while the reciprocal refines.
Register the low product bits directly from the DSP on pass 6. The next
cycle can compare P with A-B while forming both candidate remainders.

Fold sign restoration into those two parallel differences. For sign
flag n, form X + ~P + (1-n) for X equal to A and A-B. XOR the selected
word with a mask of n. This gives X-P for a positive result and P-X for
a negative result. Compute the adjacent quotient on pass 6 so DIV and
REM share the final XOR. All arithmetic on result words wraps at 32 bits.

The scratch implementation completed ten CoreMark iterations in
3,081,605 bracketed cycles with both buses stalling and all five CRCs
correct. Gowin placements 0, 1 and 2 reached 83.100, 87.580 and
87.580 MHz. The median gives 284.20 iterations/s, 4.71% above 271.43.
The promotion threshold is 283.92 iterations/s, so the timing margin
for an independent implementation is narrow. Placement 0 used 3,601
logic cells and 1,078 registers, up 15 and 65 respectively, with the
same four DSPs and 13 block RAMs. On the median placement the longest
path now runs from the resolved load-buffer row to MEM/WB write data.

The prototype passed 30 ALU cases, including the proposed boundary test,
39 pipeline cases and all 53 fast ALTOPS formal checks. It matched
reference retirement on selftest and three random programs with and
without bus stalls. A bit-vector equivalence check found no difference
from the existing 32-bit correction for any P <= A, taking P = 0 for B = 0.

title: Pipeline division with one Newton step from an 18-bit reciprocal seed
motivation:
Gowin placement 1 reproduces the champion's 83.645 MHz median. Its two
longest paths run from the divider seed ROM to residual_q[31] in 17.250 ns
and from residual_q to the signed result register in 17.244 ns. Ten
CoreMark iterations take 3,081,605 bracketed cycles and execute no divides.
At that cycle count the acceptance threshold is about 87.49 MHz.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the shared 36-by-36 Newton feedback engine with a feed-forward
divider. Small divisors normalize exactly onto a 1,024-entry grid. Large
divisors can fall between grid points, but their quotients are smaller.
Together these properties allow one refinement from an 18-bit seed and
one exact residual correction. Both refinement multipliers then have an
18-bit input suitable for the FPGA's native multiplier blocks.

On issue capture unsigned magnitudes A and B and the requested signs.
For nonzero B let k=floor(log2 B), N=B<<(31-k), D=N/2^31 and S=2^34.
Pass 0 normalizes in groups of four bits. Pass 1 finishes the zero-to-three
bit shift and reads row i=N[30:21], with P=min(2^18-1,floor(2^28/(1024+i))).
Pass 2 registers F=2*S-1-floor(N*P/2^15) and X=floor(4*A/2^k).
Pass 3 registers R=floor(P*F/2^18). Pass 4 takes Q=floor(X*R/2^36).
Pass 5 registers Q*B and both signed quotient candidates. Pass 6
registers the signed residual candidates from A-Q*B and (A-B)-Q*B in
parallel. Select the corrected candidate exactly when A>=B and Q*B<=A-B.
Precompute A-B alongside normalization. Each DSP has fixed operand sources.

For r=P/2^18 the reciprocal underestimate after refinement is bounded
by D*(r-1/D)^2+2/S. For k<=10, D is a grid point and the seed error is
at most 2^-18. For k=11 and 12 the largest distance above the left
grid point is respectively 1/2048 and 3/4096. For k>=13 it is below
1/1024. Scaling those squared errors by the maximum quotient leaves
less than 0.57 quotient unit of reciprocal error for k>10. Truncating
X costs less than 0.25 more. For k<=10 the reciprocal error costs at
most 0.625 unit. Thus Q is exact or one low for every nonzero B.

Keep the seven busy clocks, backpressure, ALTOPS timing and adjacent
MUL forwarding. Implement the RV32M zero and overflow results. The
18-bit prototype passed all 29 ALU cases and the CoreMark CRC checks
in 3,081,605 bracketed cycles. Placement 1 reached 87.166 MHz with
eight DSPs, up from 82.834 MHz with a 34-bit seed and the same schedule.
Its longest path now runs from the successor RAM to the fall-through PC.
This placement projects to 282.86 iter/s, about 0.33 MHz short of the
acceptance threshold. The three-placement median is unmeasured.

title: Predict the quotient with one reciprocal refinement and a 32-bit product
motivation:
Re-running Gowin placement 1 reproduced the champion's 83.645 MHz median.
Its longest path starts at the divider seed ROM, crosses the shared DSP
and ends after the residual subtractor. The next path runs from the
residual through correction and sign restoration. The reported fetch
path belongs to placement 0. CoreMark executes no divides between
markers, so shortening these paths can raise fitness at unchanged IPC.

path belongs to placement 0. CoreMark executes no divides between

hypothesis.hypothesis:

before sign restoration. Keep the existing seven busy clocks.

i=N[30:21] and S=2^34. In pass 0 read the 18-bit constant
P=min(2^18-1,floor(2^28/(1024+i))). In passes 1 and 2 form
F=2*S-1-floor(N*P/2^15) and R=floor(P*F/2^18). Share one 18-by-35-bit

title: Cache the successor instruction's own branch target
motivation:
The champion's row for A records the last instruction B reached from A.
When B is a conditional branch, a fall-through can overwrite B's own
row and lose its taken target. Separate outcome banks in r13s2 saved
26,223 cycles but still needed EX to form and check every direct target.
The target of a direct branch is fixed by its PC and instruction bits.
A row that already identifies both can carry the exact target into EX.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Extend each A-to-B row with B's outgoing target and an eligibility bit.
For a legal direct branch or JAL at B, store the aligned in-RAM value
B.pc + B.imm even when B fell through. This takes 19 additional bits in
each of the 512 rows. While fetching B, latch the row's target alongside
the existing direction prediction. An exact match on B's full PC and
instruction certifies that target for direct-branch resolution. Keep
the observed JALR destination as a prediction verified from forwarded rs1.

Move the direct-target adder from EX to MEM. EX can resolve a certified
direct transfer with the registered target and the actual branch condition.
For an aligned, actually taken direct transfer without a certified target,
kill the younger slot, compute the full target in MEM and redirect from
a register one clock later. A correctly predicted fall-through can advance
at full rate regardless of whether its target was cached.

A scratch predictor with target metadata and the original EX adder took
3,069,283 bracketed cycles with both buses stalling and all five CRCs
correct. The PC and instruction matched on 334,111 of 343,792 taken
direct transfers (97.18%). Charging one extra clock on the remaining
9,681 gives a first-order estimate of 3,078,964 cycles. Promotion then
requires more than 91.53 MHz. The scratch version reached 85.125 MHz on
placement 1. The estimate of 299 iterations/s assumes the proposed
removal of the EX adder and target check can reach 92.2 MHz. The ALU
feedback and load-return paths remain competing timing limits.

title: Compare the resolved load tag inside two asymmetric block RAMs
motivation: On the champion's 87.580 MHz median placement, Gowin's longest path runs from the resolved tag RAM through hit selection and load formatting to MEM/WB write_data. Its arrival is 16.712 ns. Registering two writeback sources in r13s0 put another select on EX forwarding and reduced Fmax to 86.589 MHz. hypothesis.hypothesis:
Encode the eight-bit tag of each resolved load-buffer row as two one-hot nibbles. Use two GW2A semi-dual-port block RAMs. Each has a 1024 by 16 write port and a 16384 by 1 read port. On a valid row update, write 1 shifted by tag[3:0] to the first RAM and 1 shifted by tag[7:4] to the second. On invalidation, write zeros to both. On an EX probe, concatenate the ten-bit resolved row index with the respective four-bit requested tag digit to address each narrow read port. At MEM, both returned bits must be set and resolved_available_q must qualify the read. This fits in one LUT and gives the exact original hit decision. The write replaces both entire masks, so an evicted tag cannot produce a stale hit.

Use this encoding only for the resolved tag check. The early bypass still uses its binary tag. The raw data read, load formatter, single WB result, port hold enables and same-index collision veto retain their existing timing in cycles. An exhaustive truth-table check covered all 131,072 combinations of validity, stored tag and requested tag.

At 3,081,605 cycles per ten iterations, promotion needs a median above 91.61 MHz. The six-percent estimate corresponds to about 93 MHz. The timing risk is that address bits [19:12] now have to reach the block RAM address pins during EX. The champion's 16.710 ns EX result path also competes with the saved tag delay.

motivation:
The champion takes 3,081,605 cycles for ten iterations at 87.580 MHz.
On its median placement the EX/MEM arithmetic feedback path is within
0.002 ns of the longest load-return path. It crosses register
forwarding, operand selection and result selection in the same clock.
The round-14 ADDI change helped immediate addition. Shifts, compares
and logical instructions still select their operand after forwarding.

Make the second ALU operand a distinct ID/EX pipeline value. ID can
capture an immediate, the write-first register-file value, or zero
plus a one-hot claim on a producer. Enable the late sources only for

Give the issue logic the producer's registered valid and reg_write
tag. Let it claim the youngest matching nonzero rd before a redirect
squash or a faulting jump has finished canceling that producer. Check
the claim in parallel against the actual advancing writer. If a source
claimed a canceled writer, mark the consumer for the existing one-slot
replay, just as for an unverified load. Kill the consumer before any
side effect. Suppress the invalid EX writer's tag during replay so a
self-dependent instruction can reacquire its older value. An older
redirect takes priority. Hold the claim and its verification together
under data waits, and let the existing divide interlock govern issue.

The prepared-operand and shared-adder prototype reproduced all five
CoreMark CRCs in 3,081,605 bracketed cycles. Gowin placement 1 reached
88.344 MHz. Registering a new operand exposes a path from fetch
correction through the register file to ID/EX. Splitting write-through
from the RF array in issue reached only 76.833 MHz. Keep the champion's
write-first RF and move the late producer cancellation to replay.
At the original cycle count promotion requires a median above 91.61
MHz. The 6% forecast assumes about 93 MHz and few canceled claims.

title: Predict counted loop exits one visit ahead
motivation:
The champion's 64 agree counters can learn that a backedge usually repeats,
but they carry no information about which iteration exits. Round 13 saved
26,223 cycles by retaining both successor words. With both words available,
a predictor that recognizes a repeating trip count can supply the exit
instruction even during an instruction-bus wait.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Compute the direction for the next visit when a conditional branch transfers
through MEM. Publish that one bit in a 512-entry table indexed by PC[10:2].
For backward branches keep 64 entries indexed by PC[7:2], each holding a

completed runs have the same length from 1 through 30. Saturate at 31.

or index alias can cost a redirect. EX still resolves every branch.

opcode actually admitted, the registered prediction and taken-row presence.
Legal jumps request the taken row unconditionally. Pipeline training writes
so each physical RAM sees a registered index, payload and enable. The loop
counter and equality test are outside the fetch-to-fetch recurrence.

selected word to decode and the independent EX forwarding path are the
main timing risks.
